patterns.name: Scroll-linked card stack
patterns.evidence_note: The official catalog description supports scroll-pinned stacking and a receding deck. Source tabs and live motion were not inspected; implementation suggestions below are original analysis.
patterns.mechanism: Successive cards join a pinned stack while earlier cards recede, keeping several stages visibly related.
patterns.input: The visitor scrolls through the card sequence.
patterns.response: New cards become prominent and previous cards remain as a quieter deck.
patterns.layout: A single ordered column can become a sticky stage on larger screens; keep each stage's explanation readable.
patterns.motion: Map prominence to scroll progress rather than a separate clock. Do not copy the catalog's performance adjectives as measured evidence.
patterns.accessibility: Keep logical document order, provide stage links, and offer a reduced-motion linear view without pinning.
patterns.offline: Use ordinary sections and optional sticky positioning with local progress updates. Embed permitted imagery and keep all stages available without the enhancement.
patterns.avoid: Avoid when side-by-side comparison is essential, cards exceed the available height, or pinning hides reading content.
patterns.licensing: React Bits uses MIT plus Commons Clause conditions. This record contains original analysis only; component code, ports and imagery are not bundled.

patterns.name: Expandable gallery panels
patterns.evidence_note: The official description identifies expansion on hover/focus with imagery and captions. Exact transitions, mobile handling and accessibility implementation were not observed.
patterns.mechanism: One panel gains space within a compact image group, making its subject and caption easier to inspect.
patterns.input: Hover or focus selects a panel in the documented example.
patterns.response: The selected panel expands and reveals more imagery and caption content.
patterns.layout: Use a small horizontal group when width permits and a readable vertical arrangement on phones.
patterns.motion: Let expansion explain selection. Prefer measured, bounded layout changes; inspect rather than assume that width animation is inexpensive.
patterns.accessibility: Add explicit tap/click selection, meaningful labels and keyboard access. Captions must not exist only in hover states.
patterns.offline: Build an original disclosure or selection group around embedded official images, preserving a static layout if scripts fail.
patterns.avoid: Avoid narrow slivers that hide required identities, long product ranges, or essential information available only on hover.
patterns.licensing: Do not bundle or port the React Bits component. Recheck selected-version terms before any code reuse; official product imagery needs its own permission.

patterns.name: Inset media becomes a full scene
patterns.evidence_note: The catalog describes a rounded media frame growing to full bleed with scroll. Exact easing, properties and frame rate were not inspected.
patterns.mechanism: An initially framed media region grows to occupy the visual field as the visitor enters the next story moment.
patterns.input: Scroll position advances the frame's expansion.
patterns.response: The inset treatment gives way to a broader media presentation.
patterns.layout: Reserve enough room for both the media and stable explanations; inspect sticky headers and phone-height constraints.
patterns.motion: Tie the expansion to meaningful entry into a scene, not a gratuitous zoom. Keep identifying asset features intact.
patterns.accessibility: Provide the same media and caption without movement under reduced motion. Do not intercept normal page scrolling.
patterns.offline: Use an embedded permitted image/video and a local progress-driven frame. A static full-width treatment can preserve the content.
patterns.avoid: Avoid large uncompressed video, cropped brand markings, or a full-bleed transition that blocks the requested action.
patterns.licensing: This is an original description of the general framing principle, not React Bits code or media. Recheck source terms for actual reuse.

patterns.name: Navigation disclosed as grouped cards
patterns.evidence_note: The official catalog identifies a navigation bar opening into cards containing links. Spring details and focus management were not inspected.
patterns.mechanism: A compact navigation region opens into a small set of grouped destinations.
patterns.input: A navigation toggle opens or closes the grouped links.
patterns.response: Previously compact navigation becomes an expanded card-based choice surface.
patterns.layout: Preserve clear group headings and a sensible reading order; stack groups on small screens.
patterns.motion: Use a brief continuity transition without making the visitor wait to use links.
patterns.accessibility: Use a labelled disclosure button with expanded state, ordinary links, Escape handling where appropriate, and predictable focus.
patterns.offline: Implement a local navigation disclosure with in-file section destinations and no remote routing requirement.
patterns.avoid: Avoid turning a focused single-scene experience into a large site menu, or using cards to conceal a weak hierarchy.
patterns.licensing: No component source is included. React Bits' Commons Clause restriction still applies to redistributing its components or ports.

patterns.name: Manipulable card pile
patterns.evidence_note: The documented behavior includes dragging, flicking or clicking through a pile, with thrown cards moving underneath. Thresholds and physical response were not tested.
patterns.mechanism: The top item can be moved aside to expose another while remaining part of a revisitable pile.
patterns.input: Drag, flick or click advances through cards in the reference description.
patterns.response: The current card moves away and rejoins the lower stack.
patterns.layout: Make the top item legible and show enough of the stack to communicate that more items exist.
patterns.motion: Keep movement under direct control; use settling only after release and cancel safely on interrupted input.
patterns.accessibility: Provide previous/next controls, item position and direct access where needed; never require a flick gesture.
patterns.offline: Use an original small local item list, pointer handling and explicit selection state with embedded assets.
patterns.avoid: Avoid mandatory comparison tasks, huge catalogues, or hiding required products behind an unexplained stack.
patterns.licensing: This entry is analytical reference knowledge, not a copied implementation or port of React Bits.

patterns.name: Hold with visible commitment progress
patterns.evidence_note: The catalog states that filling progresses while pressed and resets on early release. Exact duration and event handling were not inspected.
patterns.mechanism: A sustained press makes commitment progress visible, while early release cancels that progress.
patterns.input: Press and maintain contact, or release before completion.
patterns.response: The fill advances while held and returns when released too early.
patterns.layout: Keep the action label and consequence description stable beside the progress indicator.
patterns.motion: Progress represents the actual hold state. Reset promptly on cancellation, loss of focus or pointer cancellation.
patterns.accessibility: Provide an ordinary accessible confirmation path without a timed hold. Do not require prolonged pressure or dexterity.
patterns.offline: Use local state/timers for an illustrative action, with a conventional confirm dialog alternative and explicit reset.
patterns.avoid: Avoid routine utilities, real irreversible operations without proper safeguards, or adding effort that serves no approved learning goal.
patterns.licensing: No source code or visual assets are reproduced. Recheck React Bits' current conditions before actual component reuse.

patterns.name: Sliding commitment with visible outcome
patterns.evidence_note: The catalog describes a sliding handle followed by running and done states. Exact commit threshold, spinner behavior and accessibility were not inspected.
patterns.mechanism: Moving a handle across a track leads into a distinct pending state and then a completed confirmation.
patterns.input: The visitor slides a handle to commit the illustrative action.
patterns.response: The control changes from manipulation to pending feedback and then a completion presentation.
patterns.layout: Leave sufficient track length and preserve space for status labels without moving nearby controls.
patterns.motion: The handle follows input directly; subsequent state motion must represent real local state, not fake processing proof.
patterns.accessibility: Provide a labelled keyboard-operable control or ordinary confirm button with equivalent outcomes; announce status without continuous chatter.
patterns.offline: Model drag, cancelled, pending and done as explicit local states. Keep simulated service outcomes labelled illustrative.
patterns.avoid: Avoid treating handle movement as authorization for real payments or using a drag-only path for essential confirmation.
patterns.licensing: Use the general state-machine principle, not a copied or ported component. React Bits code is not bundled.

patterns.name: Scrubbable value with typed entry
patterns.evidence_note: The catalog describes number dragging, bounded response and click-to-type. Step size, bounds and elastic parameters were not inspected.
patterns.mechanism: A compact numeric value supports exploratory dragging as well as precise typed adjustment.
patterns.input: Drag the value or choose direct text entry.
patterns.response: The displayed number changes with input, with a visual limit treatment described by the source.
patterns.layout: Place the value alongside its unit and the consequence it controls; reserve room for expanded Dutch labels.
patterns.motion: Feedback follows the actual bounded value. Decorative elasticity must not imply unsupported values or real-world physics.
patterns.accessibility: Retain a real labelled number input, keyboard stepping and explicit bounds. Typed entry must not require dragging first.
patterns.offline: Connect an original local pointer-scrub helper to a native numeric field and a single source of state; keep all calculation assumptions explicit.
patterns.avoid: Avoid invented business formulas, hidden limits, or interactions that confuse vertical touch scrolling with value adjustment.
patterns.licensing: The record describes a general interaction pattern only; do not redistribute React Bits source or a port.

patterns.name: Segmented appearance over coherent code entry
patterns.evidence_note: The catalog identifies code slots with animated digits, paste and SMS autofill. Internal input structure was not inspected; the single-input adaptation is a generator recommendation.
patterns.mechanism: A short verification code is presented as individual positions while supporting whole-code input methods.
patterns.input: Typing, pasting or platform-provided autofill supplies the digits.
patterns.response: The positions display the supplied code with per-digit visual feedback.
patterns.layout: Use a compact labelled group with explicit instructions and readable error/status content.
patterns.motion: Keep digit feedback brief and optional; it must not slow entry or move focus unexpectedly.
patterns.accessibility: Prefer a coherent native input with suitable label and input mode rather than trapping focus across independent visual boxes.
patterns.offline: Use clearly fictional sample codes in a local demonstration. Never ask visitors for real authentication codes or transmit them.
patterns.avoid: Avoid collecting real credentials, implying real identity verification offline, or adding verification to a story that does not need it.
patterns.licensing: Original pattern analysis only. React Bits' source, styling and ports are not included.

patterns.name: Row actions revealed by a swipe
patterns.evidence_note: The catalog describes swiping to reveal row actions and full-swipe deletion. Thresholds and undo behavior were not inspected.
patterns.mechanism: A row moves aside to expose related actions, with a longer gesture capable of a committed action.
patterns.input: A horizontal swipe manipulates an individual list row.
patterns.response: The row reveals action controls; the source also describes full-swipe deletion.
patterns.layout: Keep row identity visible, action targets readable and vertical scrolling predictable.
patterns.motion: Track horizontal displacement directly and cancel cleanly when the gesture becomes a scroll or is interrupted.
patterns.accessibility: Expose the same actions through ordinary buttons or a reachable menu. Provide undo for illustrative deletion where appropriate.
patterns.offline: Use an original local row-state model with pointer events, visible alternatives and deterministic reset.
patterns.avoid: Avoid hidden-only destructive actions, essential information behind a gesture, or swipe thresholds as a dexterity test.
patterns.licensing: No React Bits implementation is shipped; source reuse requires reviewing the selected version's restrictions.

patterns.name: Coarse image reveals full detail
patterns.evidence_note: The official description supports a halftone treatment becoming the real photo near the pointer. Exact rendering technique and radius behavior were not inspected.
patterns.mechanism: A coarse visual treatment gives way to the detailed image around the visitor's inspection point.
patterns.input: Pointer movement selects the region of visual inspection.
patterns.response: The selected region reveals more of the underlying photograph.
patterns.layout: Keep the image large enough to inspect, with a stable explanation outside the moving reveal region.
patterns.motion: Use direct inspection feedback instead of a mandatory scratch quota. Do not distort official product identity to create spectacle.
patterns.accessibility: Offer a full-detail toggle, alt text and a keyboard-operable equivalent; essential evidence must not depend on precise pointer motion.
patterns.offline: Create an original layered reveal around an embedded permitted image, with a static detailed fallback. Check asset terms before applying treatments.
patterns.avoid: Avoid hiding mandatory product markings, implying an unsourced scientific comparison, or making visitors uncover every pixel.
patterns.licensing: Original analytical description only. The component and reference imagery are not copied or ported.

patterns.name: Target-aware pointer framing
patterns.evidence_note: The catalog describes cursor brackets fitting target shapes. Exact snapping, interpolation and native-pointer behavior were not inspected.
patterns.mechanism: A pointer-linked framing cue adapts to a nearby interactive target's bounds.
patterns.input: Hovering an interactive target changes the pointer treatment.
patterns.response: Corner markers frame the selected target rather than remaining a fixed cursor shape.
patterns.layout: Keep the cue in a non-intercepting overlay and ensure it does not cover labels or real focus indicators.
patterns.motion: Use restrained target transitions; the cue supplements rather than delays hit testing.
patterns.accessibility: Keep familiar pointer/focus affordances, remove the embellishment for touch and reduced motion where appropriate, and label all controls.
patterns.offline: Use original lightweight bound measurements and local overlay marks. The page remains fully usable when the cue is absent.
patterns.avoid: Avoid making decorative cursor movement the only indication that an object is interactive, or imposing it on dense task tools.
patterns.licensing: This record contains no cursor component code or assets. React Bits' redistribution restrictions remain separate from inspiration.

patterns.name: Responsive evidence gallery with detail view
patterns.evidence_note: The catalog describes a reflowing masonry gallery with spring movement and lightbox selection. Layout algorithm, focus handling and performance were not inspected.
patterns.mechanism: Uneven media tiles share a responsive gallery, with individual items opening into a larger inspection view.
patterns.input: Resize changes available space; selecting a tile requests its detail view.
patterns.response: Tiles recompose and a chosen image becomes easier to inspect.
patterns.layout: Keep a meaningful item order even when tile heights vary; do not sacrifice reading/focus order for compact packing.
patterns.motion: Explain reflow where useful, but avoid animating layout continuously during resize or obscuring the active item.
patterns.accessibility: Use labelled targets and a proper dialog/detail region with keyboard close and focus return. Provide a predictable linear alternative.
patterns.offline: Implement an original local responsive gallery and native dialog with embedded permitted images and stable item IDs.
patterns.avoid: Avoid ordered processes, dense comparison tables, or making every catalogue item equally prominent in the main narrative.
patterns.licensing: No gallery component, packing implementation or imagery is reproduced from React Bits.

patterns.name: Dismissible feedback with expiry cue
patterns.evidence_note: The catalog identifies swipe dismissal and a visible remaining-time indicator. Timing, pause behavior and announcement semantics were not inspected.
patterns.mechanism: A temporary notification shows both its message and that its display interval is running out.
patterns.input: The visitor can dismiss by swipe; expiry is also described.
patterns.response: The notification leaves, with an indicator communicating its remaining presence.
patterns.layout: Place feedback where it does not cover the main gesture or required utilities.
patterns.motion: Use brief arrival/departure continuity and reconcile rapid repeated notifications without restarting stale sequences.
patterns.accessibility: Provide a visible dismissal button and suitable status announcement. Keep critical information persistent and pause expiry while a visitor interacts with it.
patterns.offline: Use local notification state with explicit dismissal, optional expiry and a static status fallback; do not use timers as company evidence.
patterns.avoid: Avoid transient errors, disappearing instructions, inaccessible undo windows or a toast substituting for a visible object consequence.
patterns.licensing: Original reference analysis only; no React Bits source, visual styling or port is included.

patterns.name: Segmented selection with a moving indicator
patterns.evidence_note: The source describes a segmented control whose indicator stretches and settles. Exact animation parameters and control semantics were not inspected.
patterns.mechanism: A shared selection marker moves between a small set of adjacent options, emphasizing that only one is selected.
patterns.input: Selecting an option changes the active segment.
patterns.response: The indicator crosses the gap and settles at the new choice.
patterns.layout: Use a short labelled option group; allow space for Dutch labels instead of squeezing them into fixed narrow segments.
patterns.motion: Use movement to connect the old and new selection; decorative stretch can disappear without changing state.
patterns.accessibility: Choose radio-group or tab semantics according to actual behavior, support the relevant keyboard pattern, and preserve a visible selected state under reduced motion.
patterns.offline: Build an original native radio group or tab interface with a local indicator and shared state. Comparison content must update with the actual choice.
patterns.avoid: Avoid long option lists, ambiguously mixing navigation and selection, or using a bouncing indicator as the only state cue.
patterns.licensing: This is an original description of the selection principle, not a port or bundled copy of the React Bits component.

patterns.name: Chapter handoff through a covering layer
patterns.evidence_note: Discovered through Creative Hub. The beginning of the official tutorial describes a persistent transition layer and navigation lifecycle. The text was truncated; no demo or live interruption was observed.
patterns.mechanism: A persistent layer covers the outgoing view and then reveals the arriving view, connecting navigation phases through one visual element.
patterns.input: A navigation link requests a change of view.
patterns.response: A covering phase bridges to an entering phase while the destination becomes available.
patterns.layout: Treat the layer as temporary staging above real readable content, not a replacement for normal navigation.
patterns.motion: Retarget or cancel the transition on repeated navigation. Keep input acknowledged rather than hiding arbitrary loading delays.
patterns.accessibility: Retain real navigation semantics, meaningful headings and appropriate focus/announcement changes; provide a no-travel reduced-motion route.
patterns.offline: For a single HTML, transition between local chapter sections with explicit navigation state and history/hash handling where useful.
patterns.avoid: Avoid slow ceremonies on frequent task navigation or a transition overlay that traps focus or conceals errors.
patterns.licensing: Linked demo code and assets have separate terms that were not verified. No router, animation library or demo source is bundled.

patterns.name: One set of items recomposed across layouts
patterns.evidence_note: Creative Hub links to the official Wide tutorial. Its opening describes persistent cards, named layout maps and mirrored configurations. Later text and the running demo were not inspected.
patterns.mechanism: The same items retain identity while different layout definitions change their spatial arrangement.
patterns.input: A layout change selects another arrangement of the existing items.
patterns.response: Persistent cards occupy new positions rather than becoming unrelated replacement content.
patterns.layout: Use spatial positions to communicate meaningful groups, keeping any necessary logical reading order stable.
patterns.motion: Animate position continuity only when it clarifies where existing items went; a shader overlay is not essential to the principle.
patterns.accessibility: Provide labelled layout choices, preserve focus and use an immediate/static arrangement under reduced motion.
patterns.offline: Use an original local layout map around persistent DOM elements; optionally measure before/after bounds for a continuity transition.
patterns.avoid: Avoid reordering meaningful process steps, moving items while they are being read, or copying the demo's identity and imagery.
patterns.licensing: Demo imagery, source code and optional shader work are not included; their individual reuse terms need checking.

patterns.name: Scroll-controlled phases inside a stable stage
patterns.evidence_note: The Creative Hub-linked tutorial's opening describes a sticky scene with phased grid/text orchestration. The fetched text was truncated and no running scroll sequence was observed.
patterns.mechanism: A stationary stage contains several visual phases, with scroll position acting as the playhead for their progression.
patterns.input: Scrolling moves through the stage's progress range.
patterns.response: A grid and associated text enter, expand and settle through related phases.
patterns.layout: Reserve a tall progression region with a sticky scene only when content and viewport height allow comfortable reading.
patterns.motion: Link scene changes to progress, not an unrelated autoplay timer. Keep important intermediate explanations revisitable.
patterns.accessibility: Preserve a complete linear sequence and keyboard stage navigation; reduced motion should retain every explanation rather than only the final frame.
patterns.offline: Use local sections and progress values to drive an original phased scene. No remote scroll service or animation library is required by the pattern.
patterns.avoid: Avoid scroll interception, excessive runway, inaccessible pinned content or replacing a requested physical gesture with scrolling.
patterns.licensing: The tutorial's libraries and photography are not bundled. Check exact-project and asset terms before actual reuse.

patterns.name: Preview tiles assemble into a selected chapter
patterns.evidence_note: The Creative Hub-linked official article describes preview tiles, menu hover and click-to-assemble navigation. No live timing or touch behavior was observed.
patterns.mechanism: Distributed image pieces preview a destination and assemble into a coherent image when that destination is selected.
patterns.input: Hover previews a menu item; click commits the reference's chapter selection.
patterns.response: Preview imagery changes, then the tiles join as the menu yields to selected content.
patterns.layout: Keep menu labels readable between the pieces and reserve a stable region for the selected chapter's explanation.
patterns.motion: Use assembly to connect preview and destination. Avoid a reveal so long that selection feels delayed.
patterns.accessibility: Make focus equivalent to preview and provide a clear tap/click commit. Use genuine links/buttons and move focus meaningfully after navigation.
patterns.offline: Compose local image fragments from actual embedded permitted imagery and transition between local sections; do not redraw a real product.
patterns.avoid: Avoid hover-only discovery, long menus, unnecessary fragmentation of important labels or forbidden cropping of official assets.
patterns.licensing: The article's demo imagery and code are not included. Image-generation origin is not permission to reuse its media.

patterns.name: Pointer traces a merging background field
patterns.evidence_note: The official article describes activated grid cells and a blur/threshold merging filter. Its filter approach was read for understanding, not copied. No live rendering or performance was observed.
patterns.mechanism: Nearby cells appear around the pointer and visually merge into a temporary continuous trace.
patterns.input: Pointer movement selects nearby regions of the field.
patterns.response: Activated cells blend together and fade, leaving a short-lived trail.
patterns.layout: Keep the field separate from readable content and make it unable to intercept the actual controls.
patterns.motion: Bound the active area and decay, then inspect filter cost on target devices. This decorative field is not company evidence.
patterns.accessibility: Treat the field as nonsemantic decoration, remove it for reduced motion and leave the full experience usable without it.
patterns.offline: An original local cell field with an inline filter is possible, but a simpler nonmoving treatment should remain available.
patterns.avoid: Avoid task-heavy surfaces, low-end rendering budgets, obscured brand imagery or using pointer play as the main company message.
patterns.licensing: The general mechanism is described analytically; no SVG filter snippet, source code or credited prior-art design is reproduced.

patterns.name: Semantic page with an optional rich rendering layer
patterns.evidence_note: The opening of the official Hub-linked tutorial describes semantic HTML/CSS mirrored by an optional canvas layer. The complete implementation and fallback behavior were not run.
patterns.mechanism: Ordinary readable layout remains the content authority while a synchronized canvas layer adds a richer presentation.
patterns.input: The documented scene synchronizes with scrolling, with enhancement conditional on runtime capabilities.
patterns.response: The richer layer tracks the underlying layout instead of replacing its semantic content.
patterns.layout: Keep content bounds and interaction targets authoritative in the semantic layer; avoid two conflicting sources of visual truth.
patterns.motion: Enhancement follows the same underlying state and can stop without erasing the story.
patterns.accessibility: Expose real text and controls, avoid duplicate announcements from mirrored rendering, and offer an intentional simpler presentation.
patterns.offline: Embed every required renderer/asset if using the enhancement. Preserve approved genuine spatial 3D requirements; do not silently downgrade their medium.
patterns.avoid: Avoid presenting optional DOM fallback as equivalent fulfillment of an explicitly required 3D scene, or shipping essential content only on canvas.
patterns.licensing: No scroll-rig, smooth-scroll library, renderer or demo media is bundled. Each dependency and asset requires its own terms review.

patterns.name: Recent pointer activity drives a visual field
patterns.evidence_note: The Creative Hub-linked tutorial's opening describes a low-resolution pointer-history field read by rendering code. Later implementation text was truncated; no running effect was observed.
patterns.mechanism: A small state field records recent pointer activity so a renderer can interpret its position, strength and decay separately.
patterns.input: Pointer position and speed affect the temporary field.
patterns.response: The rendering reflects recent movement with a decaying, shaped trace or distortion.
patterns.layout: Keep the trace in a bounded nonsemantic region and retain real text outside any visual distortion.
patterns.motion: Separate input collection from visual rendering and stop decorative updates when hidden; do not claim a physical simulation.
patterns.accessibility: Preserve all meaning without pointer activity and disable unnecessary motion under reduced-motion preferences.
patterns.offline: Apply the general state-field principle in an original local renderer suited to the approved medium; embed any actual required dependencies.
patterns.avoid: Avoid expensive full-screen effects without a purpose, false physics claims or unsupported GPU requirements on essential interactions.
patterns.licensing: The Three.js/TSL tutorial code, shaders and imagery are not included. No portable component recreation is supplied.

patterns.name: Compact offering opens into a spatial scene
patterns.evidence_note: The official tutorial opening describes cards with mounted, lit 3D scenes. The fetched text was partial; detailed interaction and renderer behavior were not observed.
patterns.mechanism: A compact card provides an entry into a contained rendered 3D scene rather than being only a static thumbnail.
patterns.input: Interacting with a card reveals or engages its spatial content as described by the tutorial.
patterns.response: The selected offering gains a self-contained rendered scene within the card presentation.
patterns.layout: Keep the real offering large enough to inspect; do not enclose a tiny model in dominant interface chrome.
patterns.motion: Use camera/model response only to support the approved inspection purpose. Operating a product requires meaningful object-state changes beyond orbiting.
patterns.accessibility: Provide descriptions and equivalent state controls, with a clearly labelled still alternative when appropriate.
patterns.offline: For required spatial 3D, embed the actual permitted official model and necessary runtime. A flat card reveal is valid only when that is the approved medium.
patterns.avoid: Avoid unapproved generated models, miniature unreadable scenes, or replacing requested real 3D with CSS/SVG imitation.
patterns.licensing: The tutorial's converted models, Webflow integration and scene code are not bundled or licensed for reuse by this entry.

patterns.name: Opt-in live input aligned to a spatial overlay
patterns.evidence_note: The Hub-linked tutorial opening describes landmark inference separated from UI state and an aligned mask/video projection. No camera, inference model or rendering was run.
patterns.mechanism: Live landmark results update a spatial overlay while the video and overlay maintain a consistent projection.
patterns.input: An explicitly enabled camera supplies changing landmark input in the documented example.
patterns.response: The rendered overlay tracks the latest inferred landmark positions.
user_goals: evaluate an explicitly requested AR concept
understand alignment between input and rendering
patterns.layout: An opt-in video area and its overlay need matching crop, mirroring and coordinates, with clear controls outside that area.
patterns.motion: Keep inference updates separate from general UI rendering; do not imply validated accuracy, privacy or device performance.
patterns.accessibility: Offer a non-camera explanatory path and explicit controls. Camera use must remain optional, with clear permission and processing disclosures.
patterns.offline: Low-priority advanced reference, not a default recommendation. Offline operation needs permitted local model/runtime files and actual environment verification; missing requirements are blockers.
patterns.avoid: Avoid ordinary company stories, unsolicited camera requests, storing/transmitting personal input, biometric identification or claims of privacy without verification.
patterns.licensing: Model, library and asset terms were not verified. No camera code, landmark model, captured data or demo media is included.

patterns.name: Looping gallery with scroll-linked perspective
patterns.evidence_note: Discovered through the Creative Hub entry and sketch page. The full script was inspected: infinite scroll, cloned items and scroll-linked scale/tilt/brightness. No rendered motion, keyboard path or reduced-motion handling was observed.
patterns.mechanism: Repeated gallery items support continuous scrolling while each item changes perspective and prominence near the viewport boundaries.
patterns.input: Scroll position drives the inspected script's item transforms.
patterns.response: Tiles recede or arrive through scale, perspective and brightness changes, with cloned items supporting wrap continuity.
patterns.layout: Treat the gallery as optional exploration, preserving stable item identities and a finite way to find an entry.
patterns.motion: Wrapping should preserve continuity without trapping the visitor. Perspective on flat tiles is not a genuine spatial product model.
patterns.accessibility: Add a finite list alternative, labelled navigation and stable focus. Avoid duplicated accessible content from visual clones.
patterns.offline: An original local gallery can wrap decorative copies while keeping one semantic item set. Embed permitted imagery and stop nonessential motion under reduced motion.
patterns.avoid: Avoid sequential reading, required completion states, inaccessible endless focus paths or claiming flat tile perspective satisfies required real 3D.
patterns.licensing: Inspected source was not copied. Demo library and photographer rights remain separate and unverified for reuse.

patterns.name: Continuous horizontal gallery track
patterns.evidence_note: The full Hub-linked sketch script was inspected. It enables infinite horizontal scrolling, both gesture directions and cloned leading items. It does not show keyboard/focus/reduced-motion handling; no demo was run.
patterns.mechanism: A horizontal content track repeats enough material to continue across its visual boundary.
patterns.input: The inspected smooth-scroll configuration accepts both gesture directions for horizontal travel.
patterns.response: Gallery items travel sideways through a repeating strip.
patterns.layout: Keep a clear track and make selection possible without depending on an endless browsing position.
patterns.motion: Separate wrapping from real item identity. Never consume vertical reading scroll merely to create horizontal spectacle.
patterns.accessibility: Supply previous/next controls and a finite static alternative; keep clones out of the meaningful reading/focus sequence.
patterns.offline: Use an original local finite item model with optional visual repetition and embedded media. A normal horizontal scroller may be sufficient.
patterns.avoid: Avoid ordered timelines that need an end, long explanatory text, or hijacking page scrolling in a mixed-content experience.
patterns.licensing: No smooth-scroll implementation, sketch source or photography is reproduced. Exact reuse terms were not verified.

patterns.name: Movement strength changes an image treatment
patterns.evidence_note: The complete Hub-linked sketch script was inspected. Mouse position drives image offset/rotation and recent movement drives displacement strength. The script continuously updates and has no inspected touch/keyboard/reduced-motion path.
patterns.mechanism: A moving image's distortion strength depends on recent pointer displacement and relaxes when movement stops.
patterns.input: Mouse movement supplies position and recent travel distance.
patterns.response: The SVG image follows with smoothed movement while stronger recent movement increases its distortion.
user_goals: communicate exploratory energy in supporting art
patterns.layout: Confine the effect to supporting imagery, leaving controls, type and official product-identifying details unaffected.
patterns.motion: The principle is input-dependent intensity, not a factual simulation of material behavior. Bound rendering cost and stop hidden updates.
patterns.accessibility: Keep a no-distortion state, text alternatives and all essential content independent of the pointer effect.
patterns.offline: Use an original small local effect only when earned and permitted for the chosen asset; disable travel/distortion for reduced motion.
patterns.avoid: Avoid distorting official product evidence, large costly filters, touch-only targets or using decorative motion as proof of product performance.
patterns.licensing: The inspected source and reference imagery are not copied. Asset treatment and project-specific rights require separate verification.

patterns.name: An audio object's state becomes its explanation
patterns.evidence_note: Creative Hub linked this project. The first part of its README describes simulated groove-based playback and loading user audio. These are author claims; gestures beyond documented file input, physics and offline operation were not verified.
patterns.mechanism: The project's documentation links a record player's visible groove and stylus model to generated playback rather than treating the object as decoration beside an unrelated audio player.
patterns.input: The README describes loading an audio file; the full set of direct-manipulation gestures was not inspected.
patterns.response: The author describes cutting audio into a groove and producing playback through a simulated reading mechanism.
user_goals: connect object state to an audible consequence

patterns.motion: Show feedback during the stroke and keep samples anchored to the subject. Treat live-control performance as something to measure, not a promise inherited from tutorial claims.
patterns.accessibility: Offer an equivalent region/point selection or authored-path input with apply/undo controls where it preserves the brief; disclose when an equivalent spatial-authoring path is unverified.
patterns.offline: For an approved spatial authoring task, build originally in the chosen runtime and embed permitted dependencies for offline export. Check GPU support and make unsupported capability explicit.
patterns.avoid: Avoid random decoration pretending to preserve user strokes, collecting personal drawings remotely, confusing orbit with painting or implying simulated growth is real material science.
patterns.licensing: Tutorial descriptions and original analysis only. No code, shader, model or library is redistributed; verify exact repository and dependency terms before any reuse.

patterns.name: A two-state material control changes the scene theme
patterns.evidence_note: Discovered through Codrops Creative Hub; README describes a single-file WebGL 2 ferrofluid dark-mode switch operated by click, drag or Space, with optional sound/mute. Source implementation, preview, offline execution and input feel were not inspected.
patterns.mechanism: A material-looking binary control changes a visible scene-wide theme, coupling local state feedback to a broader consequence.
patterns.input: The documented controls accept click, drag or Space, with a separate mute shortcut.
patterns.response: The switch changes dark/light mode using a shader-rendered liquid treatment and optional browser-generated sound.
user_goals: connect a setting to its consequence
patterns.layout: Keep a normal labelled mode control and explicit current value discoverable; the material effect is optional presentation, unlike task progress or a multi-option selection marker.
patterns.motion: Acknowledge changes immediately and retarget repeated input. Reduce or remove liquid movement while preserving state; source physics, duration and performance are unverified.
patterns.accessibility: Use native checkbox/switch semantics, visible focus, touch and keyboard operation, sufficient contrast in both modes and independent audio controls. No essential feedback may require sound.
patterns.offline: An original single-file implementation can embed needed code for requested offline export; verify the exported file and WebGL capability rather than trusting the README's portability claim.
patterns.avoid: Avoid shader-heavy routine settings without benefit, audio without control, a fake physical-fluid claim or replacing the approved meaningful task with theme switching.
patterns.licensing: Repository declares MIT; no HTML, shaders, audio code or artwork is bundled. Recheck exact-version terms and preserve notices if any material is later reused.
